_comment: Per-commit pin file for scripts\hermes-update.cmd. action='keep' means re-apply after the update; action='push' means commit was already pushed to fork upstream (skip the cherry-pick); action='discard' means commit is no longer needed (already in upstream main).
_reconciled: 2026-09-28 (second pass, after the 5,727-commit jump to upstream/main). The previous 12 entries were stale in two directions and would have re-conflicted on the next update. Landed entries were REMOVED rather than re-pinned: cherry-picks are now in main's own history, and two of them (6185a207ad, f672142f23) are NOT patch-id-equivalent after landing, so the tool would have retried and re-conflicted them. The rest are marked discard so the tool skips them cleanly instead of fighting. History: config.toml.20260928-pre-reconcile.bak holds the 12-entry version.

commits.note: chore: apply 11 local fix(es) from pins after update - squashed bundle of the 11 pre-squash pin fixes. Never landed: conflicts wholesale against current upstream. Its one genuinely load-bearing piece, PowerShell command quoting, was re-implemented by hand in local.py (_quote_windows_powershell_command, verified absent from upstream/main). The rest were desktop/tips/kanban/YAML conveniences scoped out deliberately.

fix(windows): normalize path separators in _check_sensitive_path and guard POSIX mode test. Never landed - conflicts against upstream's restructured tools/. Scoped out deliberately; it is a safety guard, not the terminal path fix, so it does not affect the /c/... or PowerShell-quoting classes that were re-implemented by hand.

fix(desktop/windows): normalize spaced git path to 8.3 short path and guard stdout/stderr against EPIPE. Never landed - conflicts against upstream's restructured apps/desktop/electron. Scoped out deliberately; desktop-shell only, unrelated to the agent terminal fixes.

fix(scripts): add explicit utf-8 encoding in update_from_pins (Windows footgun gate). Never landed - conflicts against upstream's version of that script. Scoped out deliberately: hermes-update.cmd copies its scripts from %TEMP%\hermes-update-runner, so a mangled read there is recoverable, and the file is ASCII-safe in practice.
